questions.q: What is the body's weight point, as described in lesson 1?
a: The weight the brain defends by adjusting hunger and metabolism
The weight shown on the scale after a full night's sleep
The maximum weight a person can safely carry
The weight at which the body stops producing insulin
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the brain holds an ideal weight and changes hunger and metabolism to protect it.

questions.q: What did the study comparing meal timing find?
a: People who ate most calories earlier in the day lost more weight
People who skipped breakfast lost the most weight overall
Meal timing made no difference compared with calorie counting
People who ate large dinners burned more fat overnight
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes two groups and says the earlier eaters lost significantly more.

questions.q: Why does constant snacking work against weight loss?
a: It keeps insulin elevated, so the body stays in fat-storing mode
It raises leptin so the brain stops registering fullness
It lowers cortisol and slows the metabolism
It makes the weight point rise permanently
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends three meals a day and limited snacking for this reason.

questions.q: How does poor sleep make losing weight harder?
a: It disrupts hunger signals, raises cortisol and reduces fat burning
It increases muscle mass and therefore total body weight
It makes people less likely to eat processed food
It slows digestion so fewer calories are absorbed
questions.why: Lesson 2 says short sleep increases cravings and stress hormones while lowering fat burn.

questions.q: What is the Japanese practice of hara hachi bu?
a: Eating until you are about 80 percent full
Eating only until you feel completely satisfied
Fasting for one full day each week
Eating slowly in complete silence
questions.why: Lesson 3 presents it as a custom of stopping short of being stuffed.
